transcript.speech: How long are you actually willing to stare at a loading spinner before you get annoyed?
Let's break down the psychology of spinners.
This is part four of my series of building for good UX.
If you show nothing, a blank screen, no spinner, users will leave in two to three seconds.
But here's the thing: you should never show a spinner if something will take less than a second to load.
One second is not enough time to show the full animation.
Because then it just flashes on the screen and the user's brain registers like 'something weird just happened'.
You actually make it feel slower, so if it's under 1 second, just show the results.
Okay, so what if your action takes longer than a second?
A plain spinner with no text works for about 2 to 5 seconds.
And past 5 seconds, a spinner with no text starts to feel broken.
The user has no idea what's happening and the patience starts to drop very quickly.
So you have some static text: 'Loading...' or 'Saving...', and that buys you maybe one more second.
Now, instead of static text, you show text that changes:
'connecting to your account', then 'working on it...', 'almost there...'
This is where people are willing to wait significantly longer.
Because they feel that there's action happening, even if it's fake.
But all of this works up to about 10 seconds.
After 10 seconds, looped animations just stop working.
Don't do them. They actually start hurting, the user's patience flips, and all of a sudden they're feeling more frustrated with the spinner instead of less.
Past 10 seconds, you need a different approach: a progress bar, a step-by-step indicator, something else.
And if something fails, just show the error immediately, as soon as you can.
Try not to make them wait 20 seconds with a loading spinner and then be like 'sorry, that didn't work :('.
And speaking about errors, in the next video, we're going to talk about those, so see you there.

creator_derived_lessons.creator_statement_paraphrase: Do not show a loading spinner for tasks taking under 1 second; show the results directly.
creator_derived_lessons.visual_evidence: Text overlay 'Loading time < 1 sec: just show the results' and visual representation of a brief flash on submit.
creator_derived_lessons.ux_problem: A spinner displayed for less than a second flashes abruptly, confusing the user and making the process feel slower.
creator_derived_lessons.recommended_change: Directly display results without any loading spinner.
creator_derived_lessons.specific_visual_or_interaction_change: Suppress loading animation display if response latency is under 1 second.
creator_derived_lessons.creator_reasoning: One second is not enough time to show a full animation loop, leading to perceived glitching and slower perceived performance.
creator_derived_lessons.applicable_context: Fast web and app operations taking under 1 second.

creator_derived_lessons.creator_statement_paraphrase: Use plain spinners for 2-5 seconds, static text for 5-6 seconds, and changing dynamic text for up to 10 seconds.
creator_derived_lessons.visual_evidence: Summary table showing thresholds: 'No spinner: < 1 second', 'plain spinner: 2 - 5 seconds', 'Spinner with static text: 5 - 6 seconds', 'Spinner with changing text: up to 10 seconds'.
creator_derived_lessons.ux_problem: Plain spinners make systems appear broken after 5 seconds, causing patience to drop.
creator_derived_lessons.recommended_change: Match the indicator complexity (plain spinner, static text, or changing status messages) to the expected duration.
creator_derived_lessons.specific_visual_or_interaction_change: Add informative, changing status messages ('connecting to your account...', 'working on it...', 'almost there...') as wait times approach 10 seconds.
creator_derived_lessons.creator_reasoning: Users tolerate longer waits when they perceive ongoing action and progress.
creator_derived_lessons.applicable_context: Loading states lasting between 2 and 10 seconds.

creator_derived_lessons.creator_statement_paraphrase: For operations lasting longer than 10 seconds, replace looped spinners with progress bars or step-by-step indicators, and return errors immediately.
creator_derived_lessons.visual_evidence: Displays of a progress bar, a 5-step indicator component, and an error screen with 'sorry that didn't work :(' after loading.
creator_derived_lessons.ux_problem: Looped spinners after 10 seconds increase frustration; waiting 20 seconds before displaying a failure worsens user dissatisfaction.
creator_derived_lessons.recommended_change: Use explicit progress bars or steppers for >10s operations and fail fast when errors occur.
creator_derived_lessons.specific_visual_or_interaction_change: Replace infinite loop spinners with progress bars or step-by-step indicators; display error states immediately upon failure detection.
creator_derived_lessons.creator_reasoning: Infinite looped spinners lose efficacy and cause user frustration past 10 seconds; prolonged waiting for an eventual error wastes user time.
creator_derived_lessons.applicable_context: Long processes (>10s) and asynchronous error handling.
